rationale: A wins because it knows which stories are pitchable now, which are second-wave, and which are still missing load-bearing facts. Its best line, "Wise will roll out stablecoin settlement one regulator at a time," turns a launch into a regulatory map without pretending the unnamed coin is enough. B is solid but looser: "One of the biggest cross-border payment networks" overstates the supplied facts, and "toll booth" adds cute color where the angle needs measured economics.
gaps_in_A: "the first-market decision is the news" is useful but slightly premature because the update does not name the first market; A flags the gap later, but the headline angle still leans on a missing fact.
"Which stablecoin did Wise pick?" is labeled `hallucinated_fact`; cleaner label would be `missing_fact` because asking the question is legitimate, while answering it would be hallucination.
A could have said more about customer risk from holding a stablecoin balance, not just accounting treatment and savings.
gaps_in_B: "One of the biggest cross-border payment networks" is not directly supported by the update. £30B per quarter proves scale, but not ranking.
"remittance company" blurs the supplied business-payments update and risks sending the pitch toward the wrong beat.
"a real data point on how far regulated/institutional adoption has moved" overreaches without comparable adoption evidence; B asks for that proof, but the angle sells the conclusion first.
B misses a kept customer-story angle even though the update says businesses can hold and settle in stablecoin; it notices the absence only in uncomfortable questions.
